description:
Issue summary:
Customers (BrightTutor) observed intermittent mixed-model outputs during a scheduled canary rollout. Investigation shows the tenant's pinned model was being evicted from routing and traffic was sporadically routed to the canary variant for 10-30s windows, causing grading regressions and increased token costs.

Impact:
- Several hundred requests within the tenant saw responses from the canary model instead of the pinned model.
- Outputs deviated from expected policy (grading tests flagged quality drops).
- Customer reported potential billing anomalies due to different tokenization between variants.

High-level hypothesis: routing uses a per-tenant fingerprint TTL (edge cookie/hash) to keep session affinity for pinned versions. The fingerprint TTL was shorter than the pin commitment/lease TTL in the orchestrator leading to the orchestrator believing the pin should remain while the edge lost affinity and allowed fallback routing to canary. This mismatch coincided with a short edge revalidation spike (healthprobe + cache eviction) which opened a window where the pin didn't bind at the edge and routing sent requests to canary variants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create tenant with model_pin set to redwood-open-3b-v2 and pin_lease configured for 5 minutes.
2) Start a gradual canary promotion of redwood-open-3b-v2-quant with 5% traffic weight in us-east.
3) Simulate an edge cookie refresh / fingerprint regeneration by forcing a synthetic edge revalidation (curl to /health causing sidecar probe behavior) on the same client IPs.
4) Observe routing logs at ingress — requests from the tenant occasionally map to canary variant for 10-30s windows while orchestrator still shows pin active.
5) Reproduce locally against staging routing-mesh with shorter TTL config to speed trigger.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:05 - Support (Samantha Ortiz): Customer reached out via support chat — they see inconsistent grading results after our canary started. Attached sample request IDs.

2026-03-10 15:30 - ENG (Ethan Zhang): Reproduced at low volume in staging by shortening fingerprint TTL. Initial hypothesis: edge fingerprint TTL shorter than orchestrator pin lease. Creating instrumented trace for affected requests.
2026-03-10 17:10 - CS (Maria Gonzales): Customer confirms timeframe of regressions aligns with their canary window. They require an immediate mitigation while we investigate root cause.

2026-03-11 09:22 - SRE (Ibrahim Noor): Noted a spike in edge revalidation logs around the same timestamps (healthprobe flapping due to noisy healthcheck cluster). Working with infra to stabilize probes.
2026-03-12 11:48 - ENG (Ethan Zhang): Rolled temporary config change to extend edge fingerprint TTL to match pin lease for BrightTutor tenant. Asking QA to monitor for mixed outputs.
investigation_notes: Edge keeps per-client routing fingerprint (cookie/hash) with TTL configurable at proxy layer. If fingerprint is evicted, subsequent requests are subject to standard routing selection and fallback rules, which can pick canary variants if weights allow.
Orchestrator maintains pin_lease independent of edge fingerprint. There was no cross-check during request routing to re-assert pin ownership when edge fingerprint regenerated.

Observed correlation between edge healthprobe flaps (short burst of 500ms probe failures) and fingerprint_evicted events. Likely the sidecar reset cleared in-memory fingerprint cache under some load patterns.

Reconstructed trace for request sample IDs shows: orchestrator pinned -> edge lost fingerprint -> routing mesh consulted weights -> fallback to canary -> orchestrator still considered pin active. No retry/resync occurred until a new pin explicit header was present.
Metrics impacted: tenant_pin_mismatch_count, edge_fingerprint_evictions, canary_routed_requests_by_tenant increased during incident window.
Related config: default edge_fingerprint_ttl=20s, default pin_lease=5m for dedicated tenants. This mismatch is intentional for global scaling but not safe when pin must be strict for some tenants.

Checked for linked code changes: recent PR that optimized sidecar memory reclamation (GH #5429) coincided with timing but does not directly evict fingerprint cache; however, it lowered cache retention pressure which may make TTL expirations more frequent under load.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation applied: extended edge fingerprint TTL to 6 minutes for tenant BrightTutor and adjusted sidecar healthprobe backoff to reduce revalidation spikes. Short-term config change removed 20s->6m mismatch and eliminated observed canary cross-routing.

Permanent fix planned: (1) add server-side reconciliation during request handling to prefer orchestrator pin when pin_lease is active (safeguard against fingerprint eviction), (2) add telemetry and alerting for fingerprint_eviction_rate vs pin_lease_mismatch, and (3) update sidecar caching behavior to decouple memory reclamation from fingerprint retention.

Customer update: Informed BrightTutor of mitigation and requested validation. Customer has accepted mitigation as workaround pending permanent fix.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-2381: Implement pin-precedence check in routing-mesh to honour active orchestrator pins even if fingerprint is missing.
SRE-1120: Harden sidecar healthprobe backoff and add circuit-breaker to avoid short probe flaps under load.
QA-764: Add regression test that simulates fingerprint eviction during active pins and asserts no canary routing occurs for pinned tenants.
OBS-404: Create dashboard tile showing edge_fingerprint_evictions / tenant_pin_mismatch_count and alert when ratio > 0.01 over 5m.
Docs-90: Update customer-facing notes about model_pin semantics and known TTL interactions for dedicated tenants.
